prompt_text:
Task: Managed Log Query / Log Ingestion

Write code that writes application log events that include a shared request or correlation identifier using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Google Cloud Logging:
  Service: Cloud Logging
  SDK: google-cloud-logging
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: entries.write, entries.list
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/entries/write, https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/reference/v2/rest/v2/entries/list

Option 2 — Alibaba Simple Log Service:
  Service: Simple Log Service
  SDK: aliyun-log-python-sdk
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: PutLogs, GetLogs, GetLogsV2
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET, ALIBABA_SLS_ENDPOINT
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/2847535.html, https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/2771313.html

Option 3 — Amazon CloudWatch Logs:
  Service: Amazon CloudWatch Logs
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: put_log_events, filter_log_events, start_query
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatchLogs/latest/APIReference/API_PutLogEvents.html, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatchLogs/latest/APIReference/API_StartQuery.html

Option 4 — Azure Monitor Logs:
  Service: Azure Monitor Logs / Logs Ingestion API
  SDK: azure-monitor-ingestion / azure-monitor-query
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: upload, query_workspace, query_resource
  Setup hints: AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/custom-logs-overview, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/api/overview

Option 5 — Datadog:
  Service: Datadog Logs API
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: submit logs, search logs
  Setup hints: DD_API_KEY, DD_APP_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.datadoghq.com/logs/guide/access-your-log-data-programmatically/, https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/logs/

Option 6 — IBM Cloud Logs:
  Service: IBM Cloud Logs
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: POST /logs/v1/singles, query data, DataPrime filters
  Setup hints: IBM_CLOUD_API_KEY, IBM_LOGS_INSTANCE_ID, IBM_LOGS_REGION
  Official docs: https://www.ibm.com/products/cloud-logs

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

output_text:
import logging
import os
import time
import uuid

from google.cloud import logging as google_logging

# Set up the Google Cloud Logging client
# Ensure GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable is set or authentication is otherwise configured.
# For example, by running `gcloud auth application-default login`
logging_client = google_logging.Client()
logger = logging_client.logger("my-app-logs") # Create a logger for a specific log name

def write_app_log_event(message: str, severity: str, correlation_id: str,
                        request_path: str = None, user_id: str = None):
    """
    Writes an application log event to Google Cloud Logging with a shared correlation ID.

    Args:
        message (str): The main log message.
        severity (str): The severity level of the log (e.g., "INFO", "WARNING", "ERROR").
        correlation_id (str): A unique identifier to link related log events.
        request_path (str, optional): The path of the incoming request, if applicable.
        user_id (str, optional): The ID of the user performing the action, if applicable.
    """
    # Structured payload for the log entry
    payload = {
        "message": message,
        "correlation_id": correlation_id,
    }
    if request_path:
        payload["request_path"] = request_path
    if user_id:
        payload["user_id"] = user_id

    # Write the log entry.
    # The `logger.log_struct` method automatically sets the `jsonPayload` field.
    # The severity argument sets the `severity` field.
    logger.log_struct(
        payload,
        severity=severity,
        # You can add resource and labels as needed.
        # For example, to associate with a specific compute instance or Kubernetes pod.
        # resource=google_logging.resource.Resource(type="gce_instance", labels={"instance_id": "..."}),
        # labels={"environment": "production", "service": "myservice"}
    )

    print(f"Logged event with correlation_id: {correlation_id}, message: {message}, severity: {severity}")

# Example usage (not part of the required output, but useful for testing)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Generate a unique correlation ID for a simulated request
    request_correlation_id = str(uuid.uuid4())

    print(f"Simulating a request with correlation ID: {request_correlation_id}")

    # Log events related to a single request
    write_app_log_event(
        message="Incoming request received.",
        severity="INFO",
        correlation_id=request_correlation_id,
        request_path="/api/v1/data",
        user_id="user123"
    )

    time.sleep(0.1) # Simulate some processing time

    write_app_log_event(
        message="Processing data for request.",
        severity="DEBUG",
        correlation_id=request_correlation_id,
        request_path="/api/v1/data",
        user_id="user123"
    )

    time.sleep(0.2) # Simulate more processing

    # Simulate an error condition
    write_app_log_event(
        message="Failed to connect to external service.",
        severity="ERROR",
        correlation_id=request_correlation_id,
        request_path="/api/v1/data",
        user_id="user123"
    )

    time.sleep(0.1)

    write_app_log_event(
        message="Request completed with errors.",
        severity="WARNING",
        correlation_id=request_correlation_id,
        request_path="/api/v1/data",
        user_id="user123"
    )

    # Simulate another request
    another_request_correlation_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    print(f"\nSimulating another request with correlation ID: {another_request_correlation_id}")
    write_app_log_event(
        message="Another request started.",
        severity="INFO",
        correlation_id=another_request_correlation_id,
        request_path="/healthz"
    )
    write_app_log_event(
        message="Another request finished successfully.",
        severity="INFO",
        correlation_id=another_request_correlation_id,
        request_path="/healthz"
    )
